root_idea.summary: The root centers on the neck, especially as a bodily feature characterized by its length or form.
root_idea.development: The basic noun denotes the neck; related formations describe having, or being characterized by, a long, beautiful, or slender neck.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested nominal is displayed under the normalized dictionary citation form جِيدٌ.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, it appears in the possessive prepositional construction فِي جِيدِهَا, “in her neck.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have a long, beautiful, or slender neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb describing the possession of this bodily feature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The front or necklace-bearing part of the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized extension of the noun’s basic meaning, referring to the portion on which a necklace rests or the forepart of the neck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a long, beautiful, or slender neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival formation; a reported usage note says it is not applied to a man, and its feminine counterpart is جَيْدَاءُ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Represents the Form I predicate of having a long or well-formed neck.
Covers the Quran-attested noun meaning “neck” and its necklace-bearing or forepart specialization.
Represents the adjectival meaning of being long-, beautiful-, or slender-necked.

cautions: There is disagreement over whether جِيدٌ is conventionally restricted to laudatory use; one reported interpretation treats its Quranic occurrence as ironic.
The Quranic surface form جِيدِ is part of جِيدِهَا with a possessive suffix; the public headword is normalized to جِيدٌ.
